title: Near-Surface External-Casing Corrosion in Alaska: Cause and Mitigation

segments.text: Recently, a number of external-casing failures on a group of relatively new wells in the Kuparuk field of Alaska prompted an investigation into the cause.
The investigation determined that external surface-casing-corrosion failures had occurred near the top of the casing cement within the conductor.

The surface-casino corrosion was found to be Caused by repetitive events of surface water entering into the top of the annulus between the surface casino and the conductor above the primary cement top.

Testing of water and cement samples taken from the field indicates that the addition of oxygenated water and chemical salts that leach from the cement creates a low-resistance electrolyte resulting in an extremely corrosive environment.
The yearly replenishment of oxygenated water in this environment sets LIP an electrochemical cell that corrodes the surface casing.

Elevated catsing temperatures (approximate to 125 degrees F) accelerate the corrosion rates and increase the temperature gradient between the casing and the conductor. creating a thermogalvanic-corrosion cell.
Although damaged surface casing has been repaired mechanically on numerous wells by excavation and installation of welded sleeve patches, accessing the damaged surface casing can be difficult.
Inhibiting the corrosion mechanism is considered it more tenable solution.
This paper will 1.
Provide an outline of the extent of shallow external-casino C corrosion seen in the field. 2.
Detail the mechanisms for the external corrosion. 3.
Detail the mechanical-repair procedures used to return the wells to service. 4.
Discuss possible mitigation methods to inhibit corrosion on existing wells. 5.
Discuss the treatment chosen to stop the corrosion. 6.
Provide details of treatments used to inhibit further shallow-casing corrosion.

title: GENERATING PERFORMANCE OF THERMOCHARGEABLE GALVANIC CELL USING A REDOX COUPLE OF [FE(CN)(6)](4-/3-)

segments.text: We studied how a thermochargeable galvanic cell can directly generate and store electrical energy.

The high-temperature and low-temperature electrodes of a cell containing an [Fe(CN)(6)](3-)/[Fe(CN)(6)](4-) redox couple as the electroactive species were separated by a ion-exchange membrane that did not pass through the redox couple.
The power electrodes were located on each side of the membrane.

When the high-temperature and low-temperature electrodes were connected, the [Fe(CN)(6)](4-) was reduced to [Fe(CN)(6)](3-) at the high-temperature electrode and the opposite reaction took place at the low-temperature electrode.
This increased the [Fe(CN)(6)](3-) and [Fe(CN)(6)](4-) concentration difference between the two regions separated by the membrane.
This difference generated and stored electrical energy when there was a temperature difference, and discharged after the temperature difference between the electrodes disappeared.
A cell with a temperature difference of 100 degrees C generated an electromotive force of 0.1 V between the power electrodes.
These results indicate that the theoretical description of emf in a nonisothermal and convective system could be applied to this system.

title: THE INTRODUCTION AND VERIFICATION OF THERMOCHARGEABLE GALVANIC CELL

segments.text: The principal of a thermochargeable galvanic cell that was charged by heating it directly was studied.

The high-temperature and low-temperature electrodes of a cell containing the redox couple of [Fe (CN)6]3-/[Fe (CN)6]4- as the electroactive species were separated by the ion-exchange membrane that did not passage of the redox couple.
When the two electrodes were connected, [Fe(CN)6]4- was reduced to [Fe(CN)6]3- at the high-temperature electrode and the opposite reaction took place at the low-temperature electrode.

This increases the [Fe(CN)6]3- and [Fe(CN)6]4- concentration differences between the two region separated by the ion-exchange membrane, and these differences could supply electric power after the temperature difference between the electrodes was removed.
The ratio of the discharge capacity to the charge capacity was obtain 88% and this principal could be explained by the Nernst equation by considering the thermoelectric term.

title: Electrochemical studies at low temperatures, XVIII. Study of the Ag/AgNO3/Ag thermocouple

segments.text: The thermo-electrochemical properties of nonisothermal Ag\AgNO3\Ag cells were investigated in cases (A) without the salt bridge and (B) containing saturated KNO3 solutions.

We have found that the values of the thermo emf E in both (A) and (B) cases (similarly to the results obtained in the cases of thermo galvanic cells consist of Cu \ Cu++ and Zn\Zn++ electrodes) showing a linear dependence on the temperatures above the freezing point of the solutions.

The values of E-h measured in the case (B), if corrected by the corresponding values of 2,303 R/F(partial derivative lg a(+/-)/partial derivativet) - the temperature coefficients of the mean activity of AgNO3 solutions i.e.
E-h* - lg a(+/-) plots result in a straight line with a slope of epsilon (h) = 0,259 mV K-1, which is in good agreement with the value of 2,303 R/F = 0,1984 mV K-1 calculated theoretically.
The intercepts of the E-h* - lga(+/-) line phi (h)* has a value of -0.167 mV K-1.

The absolute standard partial molar entropy of the silver ions (S) over bar (0)(Ag+) calculated from phi (h)* is equal to 58.71 J K-1 mol(-1), which is in good agreement with the value calculated from the conventional standard molar entropy of the silver ions: 51.78 J K-1 mol(-1).

The values of phi (TD) calculated from the differences between the values of E* and E-h* measured in cases (A) and (B) respectively, are close to values obtained in the cases of thermogalvanic cells consisting of Zn\ZnCl2 electrodes(3-5).
The concentration dependences of phi (TD) are similar to those obtained in the cases of above mentioned Zn\Zn++ systems.
